findings.title: The plan polish is gated at 2 % and the cheaper point it found is discarded
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize ships a plan whose own objective is up to 1.1703 % higher than a point _lbfgsb_restart already computed from it, because _LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL = 2e-2 discards any polish that improves the prior by less than 2 %.
findings.mechanism: _lbfgsb_restart (optimizer.py:382) re-solves L-BFGS-B from the best candidate's returned point and then decides: `if np.isfinite(score) and (prior - score) > _LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL * scale: return polished` else `return best`. With the constant at optimizer.py:379 = 2e-2, a polish that drops the objective by less than 2 % is thrown away and the un-polished point is shipped. On the worst grid cell the space sub-problem's four L-BFGS-B solves return 13.508886 / 13.143515 / 13.182604 / 13.376755; the best of them (13.143515) is polished to 12.989696, a 1.1703 % drop, and the solver returns 13.143515. The cheaper feasible point is held, priced on the same objective, and discarded.

evidence.unit: percent relative objective gap (shipped vs _LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL = 0.0), max over 56 priced cells
evidence.machine: Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS 25.6.0, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1
evidence.contention_note: Shared audit box, load1 10.45-25.25 during this run; two other finders' solves concurrent for part of it. All numbers here are objectives and counts, which do not depend on the load. thread_factor 1.0000.
evidence.tolerance: +-0.02 percent (objective repeats bit-identically; the spread is across the perturbation, not across runs)

perturbation.change: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:379  `_LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL = 2e-2` -> `_LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL = 0.0`, a one-line production edit (or the module-constant patch the harness applies and restores in a finally).
perturbation.observed_value: worst cell 13.143515 -> 12.989696 (objective_value 13.143515454 -> 12.989696358); max gap over the grid 1.1703 %; 9 of 56 priced cells move

findings.metric_definition: Per priced cell, the relative gap in percent between the objective_value optimize() returns and the value it returns under the perturbed _LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL on identical inputs.

findings.title: The polish runs on one candidate, so every other candidate's polish never runs
findings.claim: _multi_start_minimize applies _lbfgsb_restart once, to the candidate whose raw L-BFGS-B result is lowest, so the polish of the other three candidates never runs and production ships an objective up to 1.4023 % above the best its own code reaches from those same candidates.
findings.mechanism: _multi_start_minimize (optimizer.py:420) keeps `best` = the lowest-scoring raw result and calls `return _lbfgsb_restart(best, ...)` at :540. The other candidates' basins are never polished even when polishing them lands strictly lower. On summer_negative / winter_cold / single zone / DHW off, polishing each candidate separately gives 12.959204 / 13.143515 / 13.182603 / 13.021284 while production ships 13.143515. The challenger is production _multi_start_minimize invoked on one captured candidate at a time with the captured args, maxiter, batch_objective and fd_eps (no reimplementation), and hooking _scoped_minimize in both modes shows the raw solves are bit-identical, so the whole difference is which candidate gets polished.

evidence.unit: percent relative objective gap (shipped sub-problem objective vs best per-candidate polish), max over 28 priced cells
evidence.machine: Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS 25.6.0, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1
evidence.contention_note: Shared audit box; run completed in 109 s with load1 11.17 at the end. Objectives only, load-independent. thread_factor from the run's own RESULT block.

perturbation.change: Hand each captured candidate to production `_multi_start_minimize` on its own (harness flag; no production edit needed), which is equivalent to moving the trailing `return _lbfgsb_restart(best, ...)` at optimizer.py:540 into the candidate loop so each candidate's own result is polished before the comparison.
perturbation.observed_value: worst cell 13.143515 -> 12.959204 (1.4023 %); mean over 28 priced cells 0.0895 %

findings.metric_definition: Per priced cell, the relative gap in percent between the objective the shipped _multi_start_minimize returns and the best objective production code reaches polishing each captured candidate alone.

null_control.note: FAILS the flat-price control, and is reported as failing. Eight flat cells: gap max 0.3781 %, mean 0.1682 % -- 27 % of the priced maximum and larger than the priced mean (0.0895 %). At flat prices the lower objective buys comfort pull and terminal value, not cheaper energy. D0-02 is therefore a solver-quality defect on the production objective, not a price-arbitrage gain; the price-specific claim is D0-01's, whose control passes at 0.0194 % against 1.1703 %.

non_findings.claim: The solver is deterministic and idempotent: re-running the identical captured _multi_start_minimize call with the same kwargs returns the same objective.
The production objective is a pure function of the plan vector: five evaluations at one fixed point agree exactly, so no solver state leaks between evaluations.
The plan D0-01 ships is feasible and no worse on the hard lines: comfort floor and DHW availability hold for both arms.
